top.headline: CNN, MS NOW and Politico Sue Trump Administration Over White House Ban
top.blurb: CNN, MS NOW and Politico sued the Trump administration after their reporters were turned away from White House grounds and had press badges seized, days after Trump said he was banning the three outlets over what he called 'FICTION and LIES' coverage. The suit argues the ban is unconstitutional viewpoint discrimination against the press.

top.headline: Diesel Prices Deepen a Farm Crisis in the Middle of Harvest
top.blurb: John Boyd Jr., a fourth-generation Virginia farmer and president of the National Black Farmers Association, says diesel now costs him nearly $7 a gallon, almost double last year's price, in the middle of harvesting corn. The national average has climbed past $6.51 a gallon, another economic knock-on from the war with Iran disrupting Middle East oil shipments.

top.headline: IIT Bombay Suspends Dean as Caste-Discrimination Death Divides Campus
top.blurb: IIT Bombay stepped up security as faculty marched in support of Professor Suryanarayana Doolla, suspended from his deanship after being named in an FIR over the death of Dalit student Sahil Wakode, who died by suicide hours after being caught using his phone in an exam. Wakode's family alleges caste-based harassment; the Mumbai Crime Branch is now investigating.

top.headline: US Threatens to Ground All Iranian Airlines Worldwide by Wednesday
top.blurb: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said every Iranian airline will be 'shut down around the world' by September 23, warning that any airport, fuel supplier or ticketing company that keeps serving them will be cut off from the US dollar system. It is the sharpest escalation yet in Washington's campaign to isolate Iran's economy since the war began.

top.headline: Moroccan Parties Make Final Push Before Wednesday's Election
top.blurb: Moroccan parties are campaigning hard in markets and online ahead of Wednesday's vote for 395 parliamentary seats, with youth unemployment near 37% among 15-to-24-year-olds emerging as the campaign's central issue.

top.headline: India Thrash Sri Lanka by 147 Runs to Retain Asian Games Cricket Gold
top.blurb: Smriti Mandhana (79), Shafali Verma (48) and Richa Ghosh (49 not out off 22) powered India to a record 216/3, then Sri Lanka collapsed to 69 all out as India won by 147 runs to retain the Asian Games gold medal they first won in 2023. It completed an unbeaten campaign for Harmanpreet Kaur's side at Nisshin's Korogi Sports Park.

top.headline: On 'Second Song,' Neil Young Meditates on the Passage of Time
top.blurb: Neil Young's 50th studio album pairs five new, sprawling songs from him and the Chrome Hearts with two reworked tracks he wrote as a teenager in Canada, recorded to tape at Rick Rubin's Shangri-La studio. NPR calls it less a snapshot than a meditation on a life that refuses to get stuck at any one point on the timeline.

bengal.headline: BJP Appointee's Arrival Sparks Clash at Bengal College
bengal.blurb: BJP leader Sayantan Basu's arrival to take charge as Bhangar College's new governing-body president triggered a standoff between SFI/ISF-backed students and ABVP counter-protesters, with police deployed to disperse crowds at the South 24 Parganas campus.

travel.headline: 11 of Europe's Best Shoulder-Season Cities to Visit This Fall
travel.blurb: Lonely Planet's shoulder-season guide pairs cooling temperatures and thinning crowds with festival season in Budapest and discounted admission at Athens' ancient sites, among eleven European cities worth an autumn visit.

travel.headline: New Zealand's Kakapo Population Hits a Record High
travel.blurb: A record 90 kakapo chicks fledged this breeding season, lifting the flightless parrot's official population to 325 — the highest count in roughly 75 years, up from just 51 birds when New Zealand's recovery program began in 1995.

happy.headline: A Garden Ornament Turned Out to Be a Lost Sculpture by America's First Professional Female Sculptor
happy.blurb: A lichen-covered marble bust that had stood unrecognized in an English garden for decades turned out to be Daphne, likely the 1854 debut work of Harriet Goodhue Hosmer, America's first professional female sculptor. A routine property valuation identified it; cleaned and revealed, the sculpture is now valued at up to $24,300 — a startling discovery for the family that had walked past it for years.

tech_top.headline: Apple Escalates Trade-Secrets Fight With OpenAI Over Hardware Plans
tech_top.blurb: Apple asked the court overseeing its trade-secrets suit against OpenAI to let its own experts review forensic images from a former employee's MacBook, while seeking OpenAI hardware R&D documents of its own. Apple's lawyers say the laptop shows a confidential power-converter circuit file being used in simulations and evidence of instructions to destroy data; OpenAI calls the dispute a result of Apple's own flawed offboarding process.
tech_top.pm_note: A discovery fight over what counts as 'destroying evidence' during an employee's move to a competitor is worth watching for how it shapes offboarding policy anywhere trade secrets and departing talent overlap.

tech_top.headline: Amazon and Walmart's Drone Deliveries Are Overwhelming a Texas Suburb
tech_top.blurb: Amazon and Walmart drones are flying more than a hundred deliveries a day over Richardson, Texas, after a no-fly zone around a hospital funneled most traffic over one neighborhood; residents describe the noise as 'a loud swarm of bees.' The city council is weighing whether it can legally claw back Amazon's zoning after the FAA signed off on the routes in July.
tech_top.pm_note: A backlash born from where a product routes its volume, not from what was built, is easy to miss in a launch plan — worth war-gaming neighborhood-level externalities before scaling any physical delivery product.

tech_top.headline: Traffic to News Sites Is Collapsing as AI Interfaces Replace Search and Social
tech_top.blurb: Traffic to US news sites is falling sharply as tech platforms shift users toward AI interfaces that answer questions directly instead of linking out, forcing publishers into faster pivots, layoffs and consolidation. Some outlets are seeing growth in 'dark social' referrals — links shared privately via text and email — as one of the few channels chatbots can't easily replicate.
tech_top.pm_note: If a product depends on organic search or social referral traffic, the same platform shift now eating publishers' audiences is worth stress-testing against your own acquisition funnel before the numbers move.

tech_more.headline: Tencent's New Image Model Claims Parity With ByteDance's Seedream
tech_more.blurb: Tencent launched Hy Image 3.5 Preview, saying internal testing put its results on par with ByteDance's Seedream 5.0 Pro, the latest move in China's fast-escalating race among image-generation models.

tech_101.text: In a lawsuit over stolen trade secrets, 'discovery' is the phase where each side can demand the other's internal files and devices — here, a former employee's laptop — to prove or disprove that confidential material was taken and used.

Traffic a website can't trace to its source because it arrived through a private channel — a text message, an email, a DM — rather than a clickable public link, making it one of the few referral paths an AI chatbot can't intercept.

science.headline: A Cheap New Process Turns Plastic Waste Into Gasoline and Diesel
science.blurb: Oak Ridge National Laboratory chemists found that inexpensive aluminum-based molten salts can break long polyethylene molecules — the plastic in shopping bags and cutting boards — into smaller hydrocarbons under relatively mild conditions, yielding about 60% gasoline. Unlike older plastic-to-fuel methods, the process needs no added hydrogen, organic solvents or noble metals.

science.headline: NASA Powers Up the Roman Space Telescope's 300-Megapixel Camera
science.blurb: NASA successfully activated the Roman Space Telescope's 300-megapixel infrared camera, which will image huge stretches of sky with Hubble-level sharpness, while its planet-hunting coronagraph also passed its own checkout. The milestones come as Roman, a million miles into its journey to the L2 orbit, moves a step closer to beginning science operations in 2027.

science.headline: An Underground Experiment Rules Out One Theory of What Kills Schrödinger's Cat
science.blurb: Physicists beneath Italy's Gran Sasso mountain spent 62 days hunting for a faint radiation signal that would confirm a decades-old theory: that ripples in spacetime caused by gravity gradually destroy quantum superpositions, which is why cats are never observed both alive and dead. They found no such signal, ruling out gravity as the explanation and narrowing the search for what actually forces a quantum system into one definite state.

philosophy.headline: AI Is Coming for the Meritocracy
philosophy.blurb: Branko Milanović and Nils Gilman revisit political theorist James Burnham's 1941 claim that capitalism was giving way to 'managerialism' — control passing not to owners but to the people who know how to run things — and argue AI is now hollowing out the managerial and professional jobs that same shift once created. It's a political-philosophy argument that the ladder of upward mobility itself, not just individual jobs, is what AI puts at risk.

philosophy.headline: Why AI Writing Feels Impoverished, Even When It's Fluent
philosophy.blurb: Writer Afra Wang argues that great writing has never come from systems of reward and punishment, tracing a line from Baudelaire's France through the 'Simplified Chinese Internet' to the reward-modeling that shapes how large language models write today. Her case: the flattening readers sense in AI prose isn't a bug to be fine-tuned away but a structural consequence of optimizing language for approval.

philosophy_101.text: James Burnham's 1941 theory that capitalism wasn't being replaced by socialism but by a system where control of production passes to professional managers rather than owners or workers — a lens some now apply to argue AI is displacing the managers in turn.

The tendency of an AI system trained partly on its own past output, or optimized to please raters, to gradually lose the variety and edge of the human writing it started from — producing text that is fluent but flatter with each generation.
